items.headline: Anthropic Just Had Its First Profitable Quarter, With Revenue Topping $11.5 Billion
items.summary: Anthropic (the company behind Claude) reported over $11.5 billion in revenue for the quarter, more than 14 times what it made a year ago, and posted its first-ever profit. The company is reportedly aiming for a stock market debut around October that could value it at more than $2 trillion.
items.why_it_matters: When the company behind the AI tool you rely on is this financially strong and headed toward Wall Street, it's a good sign Claude isn't going anywhere anytime soon, though a public listing can also mean more corporate pressure down the road.

items.headline: Here's Exactly How Claude's Invisible "Watermark" on Your Writing Works
items.summary: Anthropic published new details on the hidden tag it now bakes into text Claude writes, so a detection tool it's building can flag AI-written content. The tag weakens or disappears once you heavily rewrite the text in your own words, and it barely applies to code at all.
items.why_it_matters: If you use Claude to draft video scripts, emails, or show notes, know that pasting the raw output straight into a video description or client deliverable can now be flagged by a detector, so reworking it in your own voice (good practice anyway) is what keeps it truly yours.

opportunity.action_note: When you use Claude to draft scripts, show notes, or emails, rewrite them in your own voice before publishing rather than pasting the raw output, since unedited Claude text can now be flagged by Anthropic's detector.

items.headline: ChatGPT's Smarter "Think" Mode Is Now Free for Everyone
items.summary: OpenAI's latest ChatGPT update makes the "Think" toggle, which has ChatGPT reason more carefully through tricky questions before answering, available to Free and Go tier users on the web, not just paid subscribers. The update also adds an interactive quiz feature and a preview Linux desktop app.
items.why_it_matters: If you use the free version of ChatGPT, you now get its smarter, slower-but-better thinking mode for tricky research or planning questions at no extra cost.

items.headline: Google's Gemini Can Now Take Notes at Your In-Person Meetings, Not Just Video Calls
items.summary: Google Meet's "Take Notes for Me" feature now works for face-to-face meetings too, using your phone or laptop mic to record, transcribe, and summarize the conversation into a shared Google Doc with a transcript and action items. It rolled out on Android first, then to the web this week.
items.why_it_matters: If you run in-person client meetings or consultations, Gemini can now auto-generate notes and follow-up action items for those too, saving you from scribbling notes or trying to remember what was decided.

items.headline: CapCut's Free Design Tool Adds an AI Assistant and Sharper Image Generator
items.summary: CapCut upgraded its free browser-based Design Studio with an AI agent that works right on your canvas, a new "Skills" library of one-click templates for repetitive design tasks, and ByteDance's newer Seedream 5.0 Pro model for sharper AI-generated graphics. It's separate from CapCut's video tools, this one is aimed at flyers, product photos, and social graphics.
items.why_it_matters: If you need quick branded graphics, like product photos or social posts, but don't have design skills or software like Photoshop, this gives you a free tool that can build them for you from a plain-English request.
